# CG-REQ-026: Request pattern added

A regular-expression pattern now restricts a request string.

**Why it matters:** Patterns are compared as text and never executed, so the impact is policy-dependent.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Area | [Requests](./#req) |
| Direction | request |
| Detects | `schema.patternChanged` |
| Severity | breaking: high · potentially breaking: medium · undetermined: medium |
| Classification can be overridden | yes |

## Message

> Pattern `{pattern}` now restricts {where}.
>
> Strings that do not match the pattern will be rejected.
>
> **Fix:** Confirm that consumers only send matching values.

## Examples

Each example is an executed test case of the rule (`packages/engine/test/compat/fixtures.ts`).

### Fires: pattern added

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      post:
-       requestBody: {content: {application/json: {schema: {type: string}}}}
+       requestBody: {content: {application/json: {schema: {type: string, pattern: '^[A-Z]{3}$'}}}}
        responses: {'204': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** Potentially breaking, medium. Pattern `^[A-Z]{3}$` now restricts POST /x: the request body (application/json).

### Does not fire: pattern removed

```diff
  openapi: 3.1.0
  info: {title: t, version: v}
  paths:
    /x:
      post:
-       requestBody: {content: {application/json: {schema: {type: string, pattern: '^a'}}}}
+       requestBody: {content: {application/json: {schema: {type: string}}}}
        responses: {'204': {description: ok}}
```

**Result:** no finding from this rule.

## Limitations

- A trivially permissive pattern (`.*`) is still flagged.
